competitive_landscape: Inter-island transport is by privately-run diesel 'lancha' speedboats from Puerto Ayora — a rough, wet, fume-heavy ~2-hour open-water ride. Inside the Galápagos Marine Reserve there is enormous pressure to decarbonise and cut wake/noise.

demand_signals.label: Inter-island lifeline
demand_signals.note: The only non-air link for residents and guests

journeys.today: ~2 h on a wet, loud diesel speedboat across open Pacific swell.
journeys.with_navier: A stable, silent, zero-emission foiling crossing — exactly the low-wake craft the marine reserve wants.

navier_fit.pioneer_ii: The ~33.6nm Puerto Ayora ↔ Floreana leg is within Pioneer II range; an all-electric, zero-wake foiler is the ideal answer to the reserve's decarbonisation and wildlife-disturbance mandates.
navier_fit.quanta_lr: Useful for the longer outer-island legs (Isabela / San Cristóbal cross-archipelago) as the network grows.

precedents.why_it_matters: Proof that clean foiling island mobility scales inside a strict marine-protected archipelago.

regulatory_note: The entire archipelago is the Galápagos National Park and Marine Reserve (UNESCO World Heritage); zero-emission, zero-wake, low-noise operation is not just welcome but close to a precondition. Engagement via the Galápagos National Park Directorate.
seasonality: Two seasons: warm/wet (Dec–May) and cool/dry 'garúa' (Jun–Nov) with bigger swell. Foiling stabilises the rough open-water crossings year-round.
summary: Floreana is the least-populated of the inhabited Galápagos islands, linked to Santa Cruz (Puerto Ayora) by inter-island speedboat. Demand is conservation-grade eco-tourism into one of the most strictly protected marine reserves on Earth.
tagline: The Galápagos' smallest inhabited island — a fragile UNESCO outpost reached only by sea.

use_cases.body: A silent, clean foiling link replacing the diesel lanchas on the Puerto Ayora ↔ Floreana run — the craft the reserve actually wants.
use_cases.title: Zero-emission inter-island lifeline

use_cases.body: Conservation-grade, low-wake transfers for strictly-capped Galápagos visitors.
